tiles.c: Picked before kick-off. A Banker clears 70% in every batch and holds at full team news weight.
Mean chance the model gives its own result pick.
35 pending, 0 on one source, 0 in conflict.

p: Each card also shows Sensei's analyst card (research archive of 17 Oct 2026, record/research/): a revised score, a result lean, a confidence label, a market to assess, and a historical verdict from a recent-form, H2H and last-five xG review of all 88 clubs. The analyst lean differs from the model's pick in 0 of 35 games, and the research flags 0 games for review.

The analyst card is judgement. Its confidence labels are not probabilities, it was not backtested, and its xG figures are Sportmonks via Statz, not Opta. The model's picks, chances and Banker labels are unchanged by it.

Chance is the share of 1000 simulated games in which the picked result happened, from the headline batch, with the lowest of three batches in brackets. A Banker clears 70% in all three batches of the team news run and in the odds-only run, and the pick must not change at full team news weight. Under 55% is marked Near coin flip. The score is mechanical: the most frequent scoreline inside the picked result, with an exact-grid tie-break. Nobody edits it by hand.
Probabilities are not promises. A 75% Banker still loses one game in four, and a combination of several legs multiplies the risk (run `fbl combo` for the arithmetic).

35 games had their expected total fitted to bookmaker Over/Under prices and 0 used the legacy blend because no usable totals were found. The market-fit method is proposed (decision UEL-002) and has not been backtested yet; the blend's competition goal scales (0.90 Europa League, 1.08 Champions League) were never backtested either.

Team news is applied at half weight because the odds already know most of it. Player tiers default to 2 (regular) unless data/tiers.csv says otherwise, and lineups are not read yet, so depth verdicts are indicative.

Not modelled because position or tier is unknown: Brunner (?, tier 2) | Femi Azeez (?, tier 3); Zadok Yohanna (?, tier 3) | George Hemmings (?, tier 2) | L. Venturino (?, tier 2) | Markgraf (?, tier 2); Lathe (?, tier 2) | R. Sottil (?, tier 2)

strategy.h: What the five-season test says (8,908 games, out/backtest_2026-10-18.md)
p: The model and the bookmakers' margin-free prices are not separable: log loss 0.9688 against 0.9682. It reads the market well; it does not beat it.
Picks the model rated 70% or more won 79.3% of the time (predicted 76.7%), so the Banker line is honest, if slightly cautious.

Backing every favourite at bet365's closing price lost 2.0% per bet; longshots lost 12.7%. At Betway: favourites -1.5%, longshots -13.5%. Only the single best price across the whole market (often 40 or more European books) broke even, which a TAB NZ account cannot reach.

strategy.h: Markets, how they settle, and what we can price
p: Match result (1X2), double chance, draw no bet, Asian handicap, total goals, both teams to score, team goals, win to nil, correct score, result plus goals: all read from the same simulated score grid, so two legs on one match are priced together, not multiplied.

Corners and yellow cards: our history model beats a plain league average by about 1% (walk-forward test, 5,255 games) and is overconfident at the extremes. Red cards: no skill. We hold no corner or card prices, so the page gives chances and fair prices only.

Half-time markets, first goalscorer, player shots and bet builders are not modelled. UK bet builders mixing goals, corners and cards carried about a 25% margin in one January 2024 sample (Propus Partners via SBC News).

strategy.h: Strategies people use, against the evidence
p: Multis and accumulators multiply the bookmaker margin with every leg. Fourteen independent 80% legs all win 4.4% of the time.
Price shopping is the one approach our data supports: the same favourites lost 2% at bet365 and broke even at the best market price.
Value betting needs a probability that is not built from the same prices. Ours is, so expect an edge only where team news moves a game, and treat it as unproven.

The favourite-longshot bias is documented across European football (several theses and working papers; mixed, mostly not peer reviewed). It means longshots lose much more than favourites, not that favourites win money after the margin.
Closing-line value: closing prices are more accurate than opening ones, so beating the closing price is the usual long-run test of a bettor.
Correct scores and scorecasts pay well because they rarely land: the likeliest score in a game is usually 9 to 13%.
Staking plans and how much to bet are your decisions. This page gives chances, prices and arithmetic only.
